title: Relative tensor pullback balanced naturality
statement: Let f:X → S be a scheme morphism, and let G be a functor on module sheaves whose objects and morphisms agree with the canonical tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Write R=f⁻¹O_S, H=restriction of scalars along R → O_X, and I=the canonical inverse-image module functor [def-pc-topological-inverse-image-module]. There is a family of isomorphisms of abelian sheaves e(M,N): underlying(M tensor over O_X G(N)) ≅ underlying(H(M) tensor over R I(N)), natural separately in every O_X-linear map M → M′ and every O_S-linear map N → N′. No additivity of G, flatness, nonzero-ring, boundedness, or derived-category assumption is required.

proof.text: On section tensor products construct m tensor (b tensor n) ↦ (b m) tensor n with inverse m tensor n ↦ m tensor (1 tensor n). The R- and O_X-balancing relations imply both maps are well defined and tensor induction proves inverse identities. Module-map naturality follows from a(b m)=b a(m) and from functoriality of b tensor n.

The balanced section maps commute with all restrictions. Tensoring a module sheaf with module sheafification agrees with sheafifying the presheaf tensor, so replacing the scalar-extension presheaf by its module sheafification yields the same associated abelian sheaf. Underlying module sheafification is abelian sheafification, hence it is independent of the chosen coefficient ring. These universal properties descend the mutually inverse section maps to inverse maps of abelian sheaves, with naturality preserved. Finally transport G.obj along hG; hGmap gives exactly the transported morphisms.
